item.title: Graph Metanetworks for Transformer Based Language Models
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Weight-space learning treats the weights of neural networks as data, processed by other models called metanetworks.

Weight-space learning treats the weights of neural networks as data, processed by other models called metanetworks. A key challenge is that different weights can realize the same function, related by a group of symmetries the metanetwork should respect. While symmetry-aware metanetworks for simple architectures such as MLPs are well developed, a comprehensive treatment of transformers, and in particular transformer-based language models, is still missing. Importantly, their weight space has a richer symmetry group: beyond neuron permutations, attention introduces continuous general-linear symmetries of the attention matrices and permutations of entire heads. Existing methods for transformer weights either capture only part of these symmetries or are restricted to a single, fixed architecture, and none accounts for language-model-specific components such as the token embeddings. Building on graph metanetworks, we propose a graph-based approach that is both symmetry-aware and applicable across depths and widths. item.title: GpFlash: Maximizing Speed and Minimizing Memory for Gaussian Process Training and Prediction
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

This paper presents GpFlash, a Gaussian process library that is focused on fast training and posterior evaluations, minimal memory usage, and scalability to high-dimensional problems.

This paper presents GpFlash, a Gaussian process library that is focused on fast training and posterior evaluations, minimal memory usage, and scalability to high-dimensional problems. GpFlash was compared to the popular GP libraries scikit-learn, GPy, GPflow, GPyTorch, and SMT on a MacBook Pro and the supercomputer Trillium. GpFlash was found to use less memory and to be faster for training and posterior evaluations relative to the other GP libraries for all cases considered. For example, when using $ x = 10^4$ training points in a 10-dimensional space GpFlash required 9.6 to 35 times less memory and was 2.6 to 54 times faster than the other GP libraries for the evaluation of the marginal log likelihood and its gradient. The memory reduction was achieved by only using one matrix of size $ x imes x$ to store different symmetric matrices in its lower and upper triangular entries. The computational speedup was the result of designing algorithms to access memory efficiently, using BLAS and LAPACK methods extensively, and factoring kernel equations so that expensive exponential calculations could be reused. GpFlash was more than 440 times faster than all of the other GP libraries …

item.title: Geometric Calibration of Supervised Fine-Tuning
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Recent studies investigate the weight geometry through its spectral structure, which characterizes how the weights transform different input directions.

Recent studies investigate the weight geometry through its spectral structure, which characterizes how the weights transform different input directions. Within this view, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is shown to induce dense updates that perturb the spectral geometry of pre-SFT weights along their principal directions, potentially disrupting the model's prior knowledge. These observations motivate using the geometry of pre-SFT weights as a reference for refining learned SFT updates. We study this perspective as Geometric Calibration and develop SPACE Subspace Projection for Adapted Checkpoint Enhancement), a lightweight post-hoc method that selectively reverts SFT update components within the principal subspace of the pre-SFT weights while preserving those in its orthogonal complement. SPACE is a data-free, training-free method that requires only the pre- and post-SFT checkpoints. We evaluate SPACE on Qwen2.5, Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Llama-3.1, and Olmo-3 models ranging from 2B to 14B, across mathematical, coding, and medical SFT, as well as several SFT variants. Within this view, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is shown to induce dense updates that perturb the spectral geometry of pre-SFT weights along their principal directions, potentially disrupting the model's prior knowledge. These observations motivate using the geometry of pre-SFT weights as a reference for refining learned SFT updates. We study this perspective as Geometric Calibration and develop SPACE Subspace Projection for Adapted Checkpoint Enhancement), a lightweight post-hoc method that selectively reverts SFT update components within the principal subspace of the pre-SFT weights while preserving those in its orthogonal complement. SPACE is a data-free, training-free method that requires only the pre- and post-SFT checkpoints. We evaluate SPACE on Qwen2.5, Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Llama-3.1, and Olmo-3 models ranging from 2B to 14B, across mathematical, coding, and medical SFT, as well as several SFT variants. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) provides portable and spatially localized measurements of cortical hemodynamics, but differences in channel count, probe layout, signal distribution, and task type hinder joint pretraining across datasets.

Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) provides portable and spatially localized measurements of cortical hemodynamics, but differences in channel count, probe layout, signal distribution, and task type hinder joint pretraining across datasets. We introduce GeoNIRS, a geometry-aware framework that uses source-detector locations as a shared spatial reference across heterogeneous probe layouts. GeoNIRS compresses variable-size channel sets into a fixed-size latent representation and employs bidirectional HbO/HbR cross-reconstruction with contiguous temporal masking. GeoNIRS-base is pretrained on eight heterogeneous datasets, while GeoNIRS-large scales to 22 datasets. Neither downstream data nor labels are used during pretraining, enabling evaluation under a strict cross-task setting. To our knowledge, GeoNIRS is the first fNIRS framework to explicitly model physical channel geometry during joint pretraining across heterogeneous channel configurations, and the first to provide complete source code and downloadable pretrained checkpoints. This study investigates generalized boundary representations and transfer learning for physics-informed neural-network (PINN) estimation of spatially varying convective heat transfer coefficients (HTCs) in jet impingement cooling. Piecewise-linear (PWL) and neural-network boundary estimators are inferred from transient interior-temperature measurements and evaluated against CFD-CHT reference HTC profiles at Reynolds numbers of 5000, 10000 and 15000. item.title: GarageWorks: A Shared Testbench Abstraction for Software Simulation and FPGA Testing
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

GarageWorks is a lightweight FPGA testing framework that enables the same cocotb testbench to be used for both software RTL simulation and FPGA-accelerated hardware simulation.

GarageWorks is a lightweight FPGA testing framework that enables the same cocotb testbench to be used for both software RTL simulation and FPGA-accelerated hardware simulation. A shared abstraction hides backend-specific interfaces, while synthesizable Advanced eXtensible Interface (AXI) dispatchers provide design-under-test (DUT)-specific control and test operations on the FPGA. GarageWorks is intended for rapid bare-metal testing of standalone designs and on-chip processing logic for scientific sensors, rather than full SoC-level prototyping. The framework has been validated on AMD Alveo V80 FPGAs with several internal designs and provides initial support for AI-assisted generation of DUT-specific test components.

item.description:

The rapid proliferation of distributed energy resources (DERs) aggregated by virtual power plants (VPPs) elevates cybersecurity risk by expanding the attack surface.

The rapid proliferation of distributed energy resources (DERs) aggregated by virtual power plants (VPPs) elevates cybersecurity risk by expanding the attack surface. A coordinated cyberattack has the potential to disrupt distribution-system, bulk-system, and market operations. Existing cyberphysical defense strategies largely assume access to grid network models and operating conditions, which may not be available to third-party aggregators. This paper proposes a novel hybrid, perturbation-based cyber-physical defense for VPP-operated DERs that blends game-theoretic planning with model-free reinforcement learning (RL) under a Bayesian belief-update framework. Topology agnosticism is defined from the VPP information and implementation perspective: the VPP does not require access to the feeder topology, line parameters, switching configuration, or full system state. item.title: GaborFlow: Hardware-Software Co-Optimization of Gabor Filter Accelerator Design
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Brain tumor classification from MRI scans represents a critical challenge in medical imaging, where accuracy directly impacts patient outcomes.

Brain tumor classification from MRI scans represents a critical challenge in medical imaging, where accuracy directly impacts patient outcomes. This paper introduces GaborFlow, a novel hardware-software co-optimization framework that revolutionizes the design of the Gabor Filter accelerator for generating feature maps to enhance brain tumor detection. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on fixed filter parameters, our method employs trainable Gabor coefficients within a carefully optimized range, integrated with an EfficientNet-B0 backbone CNN architecture. The innovation lies in the synergistic combination of software optimization through Bayesian hyperparameter tuning and hardware efficiency through precision-optimized multipliers. Our GF baseline accelerator achieves remarkable results, with 98.6% classification accuracy, 28.08% power benefits, and 48.83% footprint savings compared to state-of-the-art implementations, demonstrating that medical AI can be both highly accurate and energy-efficient. The hardware design files are made freely available for easy adoption and further usage by the researchers and designers.

item.title: GPU Goldmines: Tunable WebGPU Kernels for Edge LLM Inference
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF / 每日精选

研究问题：WebGPU 提供跨平台可移植性与浏览器可达性，但同一实现难以在不同设备上保持高性能，如何兼顾？

方法：提出 GPU Goldmines 框架，用于指定、执行与调优 WebGPU 内核，并以矩阵乘、矩阵向量乘、flash attention 三个 LLM 关键算子实例化；在多设备、多形状、多浏览器上刻画性能并建库，加速后续自动调优与配置选择。

关键数字：取自 Llama 与 Qwen 的形状上，矩阵乘内核几何均值分别超 ONNX Runtime 7.0 倍、超 llama.cpp WebGPU 内核 1.41 倍；聊天负载下 llama.cpp prefill 阶段端到端提升 1.48 倍。

为什么值得看：为边缘 LLM 推理提供可调优的可移植内核方案，直击跨平台与高性能难兼得的痛点。

item.title: GIFT-Eval-CTX: A Benchmark For Contextual Forecasting Model Evaluation
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Contextual forecasting seeks to improve time series forecasting by incorporating forward-looking information, such as planned events, external conditions, and expert expectations.

Contextual forecasting seeks to improve time series forecasting by incorporating forward-looking information, such as planned events, external conditions, and expert expectations. However, reliable evaluation remains difficult: existing benchmarks often have limited domain coverage, lack standardized history-future splits, or provide text that is not guaranteed to inform the future. We introduce GIFT-Eval-CTX, a benchmark that isolates whether forecasting methods can translate verified future information into accurate numerical trajectories. Built upon GIFT-Eval, GIFT-Eval-CTX contains 10,000 instances across 20 datasets. Each instance provides structured effects derived from the realized future: Macro effects describe horizon-wide behavior, while Micro effects specify localized changes. We construct these annotations with an agentic pipeline combining LLM-based discovery and deterministic code validation. We benchmark TSFMs, frontier LLMs, and tool-using agentic systems. The results show that structured effects reduce aggregate relative MASE by 40.7% for GPT-5.6 Sol and 29.6% for Claude Opus 4.8 relative to history-only prompting. 研究问题 现有 SVD 低秩压缩主要针对多选评测，生成任务常掉点，秩分配也多靠启发式。

方法 GA-SVD：① 生成感知权重白化（GAWW），利用在线策略蒸馏的梯度构造对齐生成行为的白化变换；② 进化式全局秩分配，在给定压缩比下搜索逐层秩。

为什么值得看 SVD 压缩长期被诟病"评测友好、生成掉点"，这篇用生成感知优化正面补上这块短板。

item.title: FunDM: Cheap & Label-Free Decision Models from Frozen Language Models
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Decision models such as Jev score candidate answers or actions.

Decision models such as Jev score candidate answers or actions. A small decision head trained label-free can recover about 99% of a frozen language model's multiple-choice accuracy while using only two-thirds of its transformer layers. It learns the full model's answer probabilities with KL divergence, without correct-answer labels for training. One backbone pass reads the question and all options together; the head returns probabilities for every option. We call this model FunDM (Fun Decision Model). Using 24 of Qwen3-8B's 36 layers and skipping the LM head, its +1T variant reaches 75.0% mean accuracy over eight benchmarks, versus 75.7% for the full model. On MMLU-Pro, both heads achieve 1.56 to 1.57 times batched vLLM throughput with about one-third lower peak GPU allocator memory. Both heads score higher than released Contrastive Language Models (CLM), fine-tuned CLM, and CLM-shaped heads trained from scratch on the eight multiple-choice benchmarks and coding-agent selection. Separately trained agent heads learn judge probabilities without pass/fail labels and select passing runs for 74.4 to 74.6 of 100 held-out tasks on average, versus 74 for the full-model judge and 52.0 for a…

A platform that post-trains one base model for many business lines often has more lines than experts it can maintain, so lines must share experts, yet lines seldom come with a taxonomy saying which should share.

A platform that post-trains one base model for many business lines often has more lines than experts it can maintain, so lines must share experts, yet lines seldom come with a taxonomy saying which should share. We ask whether transfer probes (train on one source, measure paired changes on all sources) can discover a grouping when the standard one is unknown. To test probes against a reference, we use seven public sources that do have a label tree (five mathematics subfields and two kinds of programming, standing in for business lines) and treat the tree's grouping as a label reference that the evaluator holds and the method does not. With four LoRA experts under fixed per-source exposure and per-expert budgets, we compare a purely probe-derived grouping and an uninformed uniform default (whose tied routing serves every line from one expert) against this reference. Deleting singular components offers a precise way to remove a capability from a language model, yet the first-order spectral saliency used to rank components predicts only a local loss change, whereas deletion is a finite intervention.

Deleting singular components offers a precise way to remove a capability from a language model, yet the first-order spectral saliency used to rank components predicts only a local loss change, whereas deletion is a finite intervention. In this paper, we study how prediction error affects selective editing, where selective editing requires degradation of a target task while preserving others. We decompose the error into derivative transfer across item splits and nonlinear response along the deletion path. We establish that outer interval screening retains every feasible candidate when every candidate's intervals contain its finite validation loss changes on every task. We evaluate these effects using one answer-only negative log-likelihood objective for search, validation, and test, with disjoint calibration and evaluation masks. item.title: From Parallel to Sequential: Small-Batch Noise Restores Simplicity Bias of Muon
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Simplicity bias, which can arise from sequential feature learning during training, has been proposed as a general explanation for the success of deep learning.

Simplicity bias, which can arise from sequential feature learning during training, has been proposed as a general explanation for the success of deep learning. An important driver of this phenomenon is saddle-to-saddle behavior, in which the gradient flow trajectory remains close to a sequence of saddle manifolds while learning one feature at a time. However, Muon, a state-of-the-art optimizer based on spectral descent, does not exhibit such dynamics in the full-batch setting and instead learns features in parallel. How is it then that Muon is so successful in deep learning settings? We show that stochastic gradient noise fundamentally changes this behavior: small-batch noise restores sequential feature learning, providing a mechanism for simplicity bias that is absent from full-batch Muon. We explain this transition through stochastic smoothing of the spectral descent operator underlying Muon. When gradients are small relative to the noise scale, the expected spectral update becomes approximately proportional to the actual gradient, which restores gradient-flow-like dynamics. We formalize this mechanism for deep linear models by deriving the effective continuous dynamics of noisy …

item.title: From Nominal Capacity to Deliverable Compute: Design, Calibration and Validation of the D-PIN SCU Dynamic Metering System
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Nominal chip specifications do not capture the compute deliverable by heterogeneous distributed networks under communication, runtime and verification constraints.

Nominal chip specifications do not capture the compute deliverable by heterogeneous distributed networks under communication, runtime and verification constraints. We formalize D-PIN Standardized Compute Units (D-PIN SCU) as a dynamic metering system for deliverable compute. The system combines five-dimensional resource normalization with topology-aware and runtime-corrected metering. A cluster-scale Roofline model yields a closed-form communication ridge, while runtime factors describe thermal, fault and load effects. We show that runtime deviations cannot be identified from nominal specifications alone. Uniform re-anchoring preserves relative metering results, and a simplex-constrained calibration algorithm estimates resource weights. The framework couples Proof-of-Physical-Work verification to a no-arbitrage condition for over-claiming and electricity-aware pricing. An end-to-end recomputation on the Zhangjiang Science Gate production node covers ten heterogeneous 8-GPU servers totaling 59.5 D-PIN SCU. Billed throughput of approximately 33,000 D-PIN SCU-hours is consistent with the physical upper bound at 78% utilization over 720 hours. Derived metrics are 3.02 kW per D-PIN SCU …

item.title: FreeSolo: Linear-time Sparse Attention with Zero-Shot Length Extrapolation
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Linear-time sequence models typically store long-context information in a recurrent state.

Linear-time sequence models typically store long-context information in a recurrent state. A fixed-size state limits how much information can be stored, while hybrid architectures that add full attention for better recall incur quadratic sequence cost. Alternatively, sparse attention with continued pretraining (CPT) can extend the effective context length. Generalization beyond the trained length remains challenging, however, and CPT can be costly. We introduce FreeSolo, a native sparse attention mechanism with a short-range sliding window branch and a long-range branch that selects keypoint cells for direct token attention. Its linear-time variant, FS-L, learns to prune the prefix before query-dependent selection through short CPT. FS-B searches balanced trees with $O(N\log^2 N)$ algorithmic cost including radix-sort construction. FreeSolo demonstrates better zero-shot length extrapolation than the baselines without long-context fine-tuning.

以上为 arXiv 摘要节选，中文省流版整理中。

item.title: Formal-Verification-Guided Bayesian Optimization for Non-Intrusive Last-Mile Coverage Closure
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Last-mile functional coverage closure for modern chip designs remains costly because a mature UVM environment exposes many controls while direct hits on the remaining bins are sparse.

Last-mile functional coverage closure for modern chip designs remains costly because a mature UVM environment exposes many controls while direct hits on the remaining bins are sparse. We present a non-intrusive workflow that closes pre-defined bins in an existing, human-authored functional coverage model; it does not synthesize verification objectives from the design specification. The workflow first uses abstract-syntax-tree (AST) parsing and cone-of-influence (COI) tracing to map each residual target to existing testbench knobs. Under a matched 20-simulation budget, Bayesian optimization (BO) is compared with continued constrained-random verification (CRV) and random search over the same AST/COI-reduced space. Formal reachability then removes only targets supported by complete unreachability proofs, after which retained targets are grouped by formal difficulty and processed by group-specific BO under a second matched 20-simulation budget. Cleanup and grouping never add numerator bins; only simulator coverage artifacts do. On OpenTitan AES, first-pass reduced-space BO reaches 241/271 bins; formal cleanup removes two denominator bins; the integrated post-cleanup stage - difficulty …

item.title: Focus on What You Need: Global-to-Local Dynamic Attention for Multimodal Sarcasm Detection
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Multimodal sarcasm detection has attracted increasing attention due to the widespread use of images and text on social media platforms.

Multimodal sarcasm detection has attracted increasing attention due to the widespread use of images and text on social media platforms. Existing studies generally treat the semantic or emotional inconsistency between images and text as a key cue for identifying sarcastic expressions. However, images in real-world scenarios often contain multiple visual objects, many of which are irrelevant to sarcasm-related semantics. Such redundant visual information may introduce noise during cross-modal interaction, distracting models from focusing on critical sarcasm cues and potentially leading to inaccurate predictions. To address this issue, we propose GLDA (Global-to-Local Dynamic Attention), a multimodal sarcasm detection framework that models cross-modal interactions from a global-to-local perspective. Specifically, GLDA first employs a global multimodal fusion module to capture high-level semantic interactions between visual and textual modalities, enabling the model to identify coarse-grained cross-modal inconsistencies. item.title: FlashT2S: GPU-Accelerated Tensor-to-Spike Conversion Operators for Heterogeneous Neuromorphic LLM Backends
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Artificial intelligence faces two growing challenges: computational bottlenecks and energy inefficiency inherent to the von Neumann architecture.

Artificial intelligence faces two growing challenges: computational bottlenecks and energy inefficiency inherent to the von Neumann architecture. Neuromorphic computing offers a promising alternative, yet its immature ecosystem still relies on conventional systems for data supply, requiring efficient conversion between tensor and spike dataflow. We observe a clear mismatch, where data conversion is slow while downstream computation is fast. As data size grows quadratically with large language models, this mismatch becomes a major bottleneck. In this work, we examine the data-conversion components that appear on the critical path of training and inference in neuromorphic LLMs. The work presents FlashT2S (Flash Tensor-to-Spike): GPU-Accelerated Tensor-to-Spike Conversion Operators, which applies architecture-aware and data-centric optimizations to reduce conversion latency. Experimental results show that FlashT2S delivers an average speedup of 850.78x over the native operators across individual operators and 802.83x in realistic workloads. Additionally, compared with GPU kernels automatically generated by torch.compile, our kernels achieve 5-11x speedups. Notably, it achieves near-op…

item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF / 每日精选

研究问题 长上下文训练把结构化注意力掩码与多节点上下文并行耦合，掩码成为主要瓶颈。

方法 FlashMask-3 在 FlashAttention-3 的 TMA/WGMMA 流水线上做掩码感知 Hopper 内核（三角色 warp 专精化），分布式扩展实现零通信掩码定位、稀疏感知负载均衡（HCC-IPO）与掩码驱动的计算通信重叠。

关键数字 单 H100、4K~128K、12 种掩码下，TFLOPs 较 FlashMask/FlexAttention/MagiAttention 分别提升 45~141%/34~71%/2~44%；并行度 4~32 时吞吐较 Megatron-Core CP ring 提升 1.80~3.71 倍；128 张 H100 训练 118B-A14B MoE 端到端提升 7.3~11.0%。

为什么值得看 把"结构化掩码+上下文并行"做实的工程重器，Hopper 专项优化与大模型实测兼备。

item.title: Federated Coreset Subsampling for Distributed Memory Banks
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

In real-world scenarios, industrial processes can span multiple factories and goods are often produced at multiple sites, leading to a shared yet non-identical distribution of data across locations.

In real-world scenarios, industrial processes can span multiple factories and goods are often produced at multiple sites, leading to a shared yet non-identical distribution of data across locations. To address this, we propose two federated approaches for i) combining existing coresets (Double Subsampling) and ii) creating new coresets (Federated Subsampling) in a distributed anomaly detection setting. In particular, we adapt the memory bank based PatchCore algorithm to a federated setting, resulting in increased cold-start performance, resilience to domain- and sensor-shift, and resilience to unreliable actor participation, a common problem in classical, network based federated learning strategies.

item.title: FedLoRD: Personalized Federated Learning based on Low-Rank Structures of Model Parameter Differences
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

We propose FedLoRD, a personalized federated learning (PFL) method based on the low-rank structure of the differences between the global and personalized model parameters.

We propose FedLoRD, a personalized federated learning (PFL) method based on the low-rank structure of the differences between the global and personalized model parameters. PFL is a branch of federated learning that aims to learn models tailored to the local data of each client under biased local data distributions. In its local training, each client learns a personalized model by regularizing the difference between its model parameters and the global ones sent from the server. The regularization function needs to be designed with priors on the model parameter difference; however, the existing PFL methods rely on empirical choices (e.g., $\ell_1$- and $\ell_2$-norms), which do not take into account the actual characteristics of the difference. The resulting mismatch of priors can lead to suboptimal personalized models. To address this issue, we propose a PFL method whose regularizer is built on an observed characteristic of the model parameter differences: they are approximately low-rank at every layer. In our method, we first formulate a local training problem with nuclear norm regularization on the layer-wise differences. We further rewrite this problem via the factorized represen…

item.title: FastEEP: Fast Intra-Instance Elastic Scaling for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF / 每日精选

研究问题：LLM 负载高度动态，MoE 服务需频繁伸缩容量，但现有引擎靠销毁重建实例来调整专家并行，开销巨大。

方法：FastEEP 基于"部分复用"原则，把可复用的执行结构（worker 执行、GPU 内存、通信状态）与当前 EP 配置激活的资源分离，协调回收与重配置，同时保留重建代价高的状态，实现实例内快速伸缩。

关键数字：相对现有基于 vLLM 的方案，跨不同模型伸缩速度提升 4.5–11.7 倍。

为什么值得看：针对生产级 MoE 部署的细粒度弹性伸缩给出可落地方案，避免整实例拆建，工程价值突出。

item.title: Fast and Flexible Spiking Network Simulations on Massively Distributed On-Chip Memory Accelerators
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Studying brain function and dysfunction in spiking networks with realistic synaptic densities pushes simulation technology beyond its current limits.

Studying brain function and dysfunction in spiking networks with realistic synaptic densities pushes simulation technology beyond its current limits. It requires simulations substantially faster than biological real-time to cover long model times and enable efficient iterative exploration, particularly when connectivity is plastic. The modelling community aspires to a $100\times$ speedup. Yet on conventional many-core systems this remains elusive, bounded by inter-node communication and memory access. So far, significant speedup has only been shown on a custom-built FPGA system. We demonstrate the potential of commercial systems with large distributed on-chip memory to accelerate brain research. To exploit the local SRAM, we introduce a group-based mapping and communication strategy tackling spike-routing challenges on massively distributed systems. On Graphcore IPUs, the cortical microcircuit runs at a record $22.7\times$ faster than biological real-time with negligible build times and a reusable compiled graph. By design, the algorithm makes no model- or hardware-specific assumptions, providing a general strategy for advancing neuronal simulation technology.

以上为 arXiv 摘要节选，中文省流版整理中。

item.title: Fast and Accurate: Improving Personalized LLM Performance by Semantic Concentration Inspired Workload Split between RAG and Fine-Tuning
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

With ever increasing personalized large language model (LLM) services, the next question to answer is how to improve the quality of services/users' experiences, which is indicated by personalized LLM generation accuracy/quality and inference latency.

With ever increasing personalized large language model (LLM) services, the next question to answer is how to improve the quality of services/users' experiences, which is indicated by personalized LLM generation accuracy/quality and inference latency. Although state-of-the-art designs, e.g., parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or Full PEFT+RAG, can help, they largely ignore the heterogeneous semantic concentrations of users' historical data and cannot fully unleash the potential of personal data for personalized LLM performance enhancement. Quantization has emerged as one of the primary techniques for reducing the memory footprint of large language models during inference. A prominent example is Quantized Johnson$-$Lindenstrauss (QJL), which compresses KV caches using 1-bit asymmetric quantization while approximately preserving the inner products required by the attention mechanism. Recent theoretical and practical work aims at replacing the dense Gaussian projections used by the aforementioned transforms with more structured embeddings $-$ such as compositions of randomized Hadamard transforms $-$ while retaining the same embedding dimension. In this paper, we introduce two constructions based on a composition of randomized Hadamard transforms, albeit with a Gaussian rather than Rademacher diagonal in the second stage. item.title: Fairness under Prediction Error in Predict-then-Optimize Pipelines
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Fairness constraints in predict-then-optimize pipelines are necessarily enforced on predicted outcomes $\hat{y}$, since true outcomes $y$ are unobserved at decision time.

Fairness constraints in predict-then-optimize pipelines are necessarily enforced on predicted outcomes $\hat{y}$, since true outcomes $y$ are unobserved at decision time. We study whether a demographic parity constraint enforced this way continues to hold against $y$, and how the resulting violation scales with prediction error. Using a budget-constrained allocation problem solved as a linear program, we show empirically that the true-outcome fairness gap grows with prediction error $σ$ and saturates, well fit by $c(1 - e^{-σ/τ})$ with $c = 0.1545 \pm 0.0103$ and $τ= 3.9045 \pm 0.3745$; its mean is invariant to sample size while its variance decays at the standard $O(1/\sqrt{n})$ rate. We derive a two-part theoretical bound: a closed-form local sensitivity result showing the gap's first-order response to prediction error depends on only two individuals per group, validated against the solver to within three significant figures; and a universal, error-independent ceiling following from the boundedness of the decision variable, confirmed consistent with but looser than the empirical saturation level. item.title: FPGA Based Design And Implementation of Neural Network Compensators for Nanocrystalline MEMS Pressure Sensor
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

In this paper the effects of nonlinearity and temperature of nanocrystalline MEMS pressure sensor have been compensated using neural network algorithm which has been implemented on a FPGA chip.

In this paper the effects of nonlinearity and temperature of nanocrystalline MEMS pressure sensor have been compensated using neural network algorithm which has been implemented on a FPGA chip. The neural network employs back propagation algorithm to train the multilayer perceptron feed forward network that causes an error reduction due to temperature upto the level of 98%. It is realized on FPGA with pipelined architecture for parallel and fast sensing operation. The pressure sensor along with the FPGA based compensation results in an intelligent sensor system capable of high speed and accurate pressure measurement which has been tested for a typical biomedical application.

item.title: FORGE: Procedural Weight Generation for Sparse MoE Inference
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF / 每日精选

研究问题：稀疏 MoE 自回归解码中，专家权重既吃 HBM 带宽又迫使多节点专家并行，能否不存储而现场重建权重？

方法：FORGE 提出片上程序化权重生成——每个 SM 内置固定功能数据通路（RGU），从每投影 O(log²d) 个转子参数实时重建专家权重，与 Tensor Core 执行互不争用。

关键数字：用不到 1 MB 种子近似每层数 GB 专家权重；5 个模型替换 30% MoE FFN 层，估计同 GPU 数下系统吞吐提升 1.3–2.8 倍、短上下文每用户解码时延降至 1.10–1.15 倍，KV cache 容量扩大 1.2–2.6 倍；RGU 在 SystemVerilog 完整实现，7nm 下每 SM 面积开销约 0.9%（0.032 mm²）。

为什么值得看：以硬件换取 MoE 存储与流量瓶颈的新思路，代价是下游精度低于未替换微调版，替换比例可调权衡。

item.title: FLAI Protocol: Decentralized Federated Learning with On-Chain Rewards and sPEG-Based Contribution Scoring
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without data centralization but struggles with incentive alignment, accountability, and robustness under heterogeneous non-IID data.

Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without data centralization but struggles with incentive alignment, accountability, and robustness under heterogeneous non-IID data. Existing decentralized FL (DeFL) systems leverage blockchains for coordination yet face high on-chain overhead, unverifiable self-reports, and weak fairness guarantees. We present the FLAI Protocol, a trusted execution environment (TEE)-backed DeFL framework that integrates enclave-validated aggregation, sparse Peer Evaluation Graph (sPEG) scoring, and on-chain settlement. sPEG incorporates peer-based quality, class coverage, promptness, effort, and reputation into composite contribution scores. The protocol formalizes contribution evaluation and tokenized incentive distribution, ensuring verifiable fairness and resilience against free-riding and collusion. We evaluate FLAI on image, text, and healthcare datasets and demonstrate parity with FedAvg in utility while improving fairness and accountability. A case study in consumer eHealth (aggregating wearable and electronic health record data for real-world evidence generation) illustrates the protocol's applicability to privacy-critical domain…

item.title: FENAS: A Few-Shot Meta-Ensembling Framework for Efficient Neural Architecture Search with Synergized Zero-Cost Proxies
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Efficient neural architecture search (NAS) requires accurate performance estimation under limited evaluation budgets.

Efficient neural architecture search (NAS) requires accurate performance estimation under limited evaluation budgets. Existing zero-cost proxies (ZCPs) provide fast training-free signals, but each proxy usually captures only a partial property of an architecture, leading to unstable rankings across datasets and search spaces. In contrast, GNN-based predictors can improve accuracy, but often depend on labeled architectures, graph encoders, and costly representation learning, which makes them less suitable for extreme few-shot settings. We propose FENAS, a topology-agnostic few-shot prediction framework that turns complementary initialization priors into robust ranking signals. Its core component, CAST, is a feature pipeline that combines copula alignment and synergy transformation. CAST maps heterogeneous ZCPs into a compact feature manifold, enabling lightweight meta-learners to produce reliable rankings from scarce supervision. On NAS-Bench-201, with only 0.5% labeled samples, FENAS achieves a Kendall's Tau ($τ$) of 0.70, outperforming representative topology-based few-shot predictors in this low-label regime. item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Large Language Models (LLMs) have been shown to be computationally expensive and vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, in which adversarial prompts bypass safety alignment and induce harmful responses.

Large Language Models (LLMs) have been shown to be computationally expensive and vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, in which adversarial prompts bypass safety alignment and induce harmful responses. To address this inefficiency, a range of techniques have been proposed to enable efficient LLM inference. Depth-based dynamic inference has demonstrated promising results by enabling outputs to be generated from intermediate layers. It offers the flexibility to adjust model behavior based on the available resource budget. However, how this flexibility affects the robustness of LLMs against jailbreak attacks remains unexplored. In this paper, we address this gap via a comprehensive investigation into the impact of depth-based dynamic inference on the robustness of LLMs against jailbreak attacks. Specifically, we make the following key observations: 1) Shallow exits are consistently more robust to jailbreak attacks than deeper ones; 2) Exit depth affects how easily the adversarial suffix can be optimized, with deeper exits reaching lower attack loss; and 3) Adversarial suffixes affect utility uniformly across exit depths. item.title: Explore with Memory, Learn without It: In-Context Exploration and Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Exploration bounds learning efficiency in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR).

Exploration bounds learning efficiency in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Current methods explore mostly through independent sampling, without fully using the information gathered along the way, such as known wrong answers and environment feedback. We propose LEAF, which injects a dynamic, problem-specific memory into the context before every rollout. The memory contains the most recent response, its reward, and other environment feedback. It is updated after every verifier call. We decouple policy updates from rollouts and update the policy through self-distillation. On four benchmarks and two open models, LEAF accelerates exploration by about 4x compared with a random sampling baseline. On unseen test sets, it improves accuracy over the strongest baseline by 1.59 and 1.83 percentage points on the two models, while using less compute than any RL baseline. These results highlight the potential of LEAF in improving both exploration and learning efficiency. Code is available at: https://github.com/on1262/LEAF

item.title: Exact power indices for plurality-voting ensembles
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Plurality-voting ensembles aggregate the predictions of multiple base classifiers and output the most voted class, with ties typically broken at random.

Plurality-voting ensembles aggregate the predictions of multiple base classifiers and output the most voted class, with ties typically broken at random. Despite the simple aggregation rule, attributing the impact of each base classifier to the ensemble's predictions is far from straightforward. That is, a single base classifier's impact depends on how it interacts with the votes of all other classifiers in the ensemble, for example, in resolving ties, and not only on its own predictions. We address the attribution problem using established tools from cooperative game theory, studying the Banzhaf and Shapley power indices for new games modeling plurality voting and random tie-breaking, for binary and multiclass classification settings. Computing power indices is, in general, intractable. Surprisingly, our methods, collectively named ENPOWER, enable the exact computation of Banzhaf and Shapley values in linear time for the binary classification setting and in low-degree polynomial time for the multiclass setting. The algorithms in ENPOWER rely on new combinatorial formulations of the Banzhaf and Shapley indices, yielding closed-form solutions for the binary case and ordinary generati…

item.title: EvolvAttack: Backdooring self Evolving VLM Agents
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Self-evolving mechanisms let vision-language model (VLM) agents continually adapt through evolving memory, but they also allow malicious behavior to emerge only after deployment.

Self-evolving mechanisms let vision-language model (VLM) agents continually adapt through evolving memory, but they also allow malicious behavior to emerge only after deployment. We introduce a new attack surface, the self-evolving backdoor, whose payload stays dormant in the initial agent and is progressively activated as the agent evolves. Unlike conventional backdoors, which can be exposed by testing triggered inputs on a static model, our attack requires both a visual trigger and a sufficiently evolved memory state; static scanning with clean memory thus yields near-zero attack success and may deem the agent benign. We realize this through memory-aware backdoor training, which couples trigger activation with the agent's evolving memory while preserving benign behavior unless the trigger co-occurs with payload-related memory. Across three VLM backbones, four agent pipelines, and recency-, semantic-, and reward-based memory evolution, the attack preserves normal functionality and stays nearly inactive before evolution (0.5% attack success rate), yet exceeds 95% attack success within 100 interactions, revealing a stealthy threat unique to self-evolving agents.

item.title: Embedding Graph Kernel Entropy (EGKE): Fine-grained Hallucination Detection for LLMs from Embeddings
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Hallucination detection is critical for ensuring the reliability of Large Language Models (LLMs) in real-world deployments.

Hallucination detection is critical for ensuring the reliability of Large Language Models (LLMs) in real-world deployments. While recent works, such as Semantic Entropy (SE) and Kernel Language Entropy (KLE), identify hallucinations by measuring semantic disagreement across multiple generated responses using Natural Language Inference (NLI) models, these methods depend on separately loaded NLI classifiers to estimate pairwise semantic similarity, introducing significant computational overhead. We propose Embedding Graph Kernel Entropy (EGKE), a variant of Kernel Language Entropy (KLE) that replaces its NLI-derived semantic graph with a Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel applied to dense sentence embeddings generated by a BGE embedding model, while retaining KLE's graph Laplacian, heat kernel, and von Neumann entropy formulation unchanged. By computing similarities directly in a continuous embedding space, the proposed method provides a symmetric and computationally efficient alternative to NLI-based semantic comparison. Hallucination detection is critical for ensuring the reliability of Large Language Models (LLMs) in real-world deployments. While recent works, such as Semantic Entropy (SE) and Kernel Language Entropy (KLE), identify hallucinations by measuring semantic disagreement across multiple generated responses using Natural Language Inference (NLI) models, these methods depend on separately loaded NLI classifiers to estimate pairwise semantic similarity, introducing significant computational overhead. By computing similarities directly in a continuous embedding space, the proposed method provides a symmetric and computationally efficient alternative to NLI-based semantic comparison. item.title: Efficient Resource-Shiftable RL Post-training with Generative Rewards
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training with generative reward models (GenRM) has become a central recipe for improving large language models (LLMs), and it is also increasingly resource-intensive: policy rollout, GenRM-based reward evaluation, and policy training all compete for GPU resources.

Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training with generative reward models (GenRM) has become a central recipe for improving large language models (LLMs), and it is also increasingly resource-intensive: policy rollout, GenRM-based reward evaluation, and policy training all compete for GPU resources. However, existing colocated and disaggregated systems rely on static resource allocation for these roles. Such allocation cannot adapt as each role's workload changes during RL and therefore leaves a role's resources underutilized. We present PivotRL, an RL post-training system that dynamically shifts resources among different roles according to their runtime demands. PivotRL introduces a resource-shiftable runtime built on a Global Parameter Storage, together with a unified mechanism that efficiently shifts role-specific context. A shift-aware scheduler enables sequence migration upon a shift, while a planner considers the aggregate throughput benefit and the shift overhead to determine when and how to shift. item.title: Efficient Preconditioned Optimization Methods with Frequent Directions
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Adaptive optimization methods have received considerable attention in recent years due to their strong empirical performance.

Adaptive optimization methods have received considerable attention in recent years due to their strong empirical performance. However, they generally require maintaining a preconditioning matrix, which incurs prohibitive computational overhead in large-scale applications. To address these limitations, we investigate the acceleration of preconditioned optimization methods through frequent directions (FD), a widely used matrix sketching technique. We first propose FTSL by integrating FD with adaptive subgradient methods under the primal-dual framework and adding back the cumulative information discarded by FD. FTSL obtains a tighter regret bound than existing state-of-the-art results. We then apply a doubling trick that further reduces the time complexity of FTSL, while maintaining the same regret guarantee. We also consider optimization over matrix-valued decision variables and exploit their structural properties to construct sketched preconditioners. item.title: ECHO: Correcting Time Series Foundation Model Forecasts with Historical Analogues and Errors
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) provide general-purpose forecasting capabilities, yet their forecasts can remain misaligned with the temporal characteristics of a target domain.

Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) provide general-purpose forecasting capabilities, yet their forecasts can remain misaligned with the temporal characteristics of a target domain. This motivates lightweight forecast correction even when only black-box access to the TSFM is available. Our key observation is that two forms of historical information provide complementary correction signals: historical analogues reveal how similar contexts evolved, while past forecast errors reveal a TSFM's characteristic deviations in the target domain. Based on this observation, we propose ECHO, a black-box forecast correction framework that learns from both sources. ECHO uses AnalogE to assess retrieved historical analogues together with the current context and base forecast, learning transferable corrections through cross-domain pretraining. In parallel, RecentE learns target-specific residual corrections from past forecast errors and refines them as causally available feedback accumulates. ECHO dynamically combines the two corrections according to their observed forecasting performance. item.title: E8 Lattice Key Quantization for Low-Bit KV-Cache Compression
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF / 每日精选

研究问题 KV cache 标量量化在 2-bit 下面临质量不稳，往往需要 3-bit 键才能保住模型质量。

方法 用 E8 格对键做向量量化，利用相邻维度相关性在相同载荷下取得高于标量量化的 SQNR；配表式非对称打分算法，注意力计算时免显式码本反量化、保持解码吞吐持平。

关键数字 统一 k2v2（2-bit 键+2-bit 值）实现约 6 倍 KV 压缩、比标量 k3v2 体积再小约 20%，长上下文困惑度接近基线；80% 的模型-数据集-上下文设置优于标量 k3v2。

为什么值得看 结构化向量量化在不损失吞吐的前提下提升"每字节质量"，是低比特 KV 压缩栈里一个低开销新原语。

item.title: DynaSPLIT: Strong tail-optimal scheduling for the M/G/n with heavy-tailed job sizes
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

We study the asymptotic response time tail in the M/G/n queue with heavy-tailed (regularly varying) job sizes.

We study the asymptotic response time tail in the M/G/n queue with heavy-tailed (regularly varying) job sizes. For this setting, strongly tail optimal policies are known only at lower load, where n-1 servers suffice for stability. At higher load, the tail optimal scheduling has been open. This paper presents DynaSPLIT, the first strongly tail optimal policy at high load. Together with prior work, this result shows that strong tail optimality is achievable across the entire stability region of the M/G/n with heavy-tailed job sizes.

item.title: DualColl: Throughput-Optimal Bandwidth-Bound Collective Communications via Fractional Tree Packing
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF / 每日精选

研究问题：大规模分布式训练中集合通信日益受带宽约束，如何在 NVLink/InfiniBand/以太网异构互连上做吞吐最优的 AllReduce。

方法：DualColl 直接面向带宽受限的 AllReduce，采用 Garg–Könemann 式乘性权重算法，用精确最小代价集合树预言机把物理链路对偶价格投影到参与 rank 的逻辑图上，每轮迭代化为最短路+最小生成树。

关键数字：对任意 0<ε<1，可计算吞吐不低于最优 AllReduce 吞吐 (1−ε)² 倍的可行调度。

为什么值得看：把 ForestColl 的分数树打包推进到直接针对 AllReduce，并扩展到本地等价下一跳包喷洒路由与无显式按树带宽控制的网络，为异构集群通信库提供理论支撑。

item.title: Drafting Agents, Not Just Tokens: Speculative Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Systems
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Improving an agent through successive revisions requires balancing exploration and evaluation under a limited budget.

Improving an agent through successive revisions requires balancing exploration and evaluation under a limited budget. A narrow search can miss useful sequences of edits, while fully evaluating every intermediate version can exhaust the budget before those sequences yield a verified improvement. We introduce Speculative Recursive Self-Improvement (SpecRSI), which drafts executable successor agents before their predecessors are fully evaluated, while requiring complete verification before adoption. Verification-Aware Tree Search (VATS) allocates the budget between further edits and outstanding checks using the predicted verified return of a continuation. Group Verification Optimization (GVO) learns the improver from completed searches while keeping the real evaluator fixed. In the main scientific comparison, terminal gains exceed Janus by 33.3%--40.0%. Additional evaluations show that SpecRSI outperforms Janus in all 50 scientific backbone--task pairs and exceeds MetaRSI-v1 by 1.85%--2.38% in macro-average system score across twenty backbones. Coding-validation success reaches 69.4% versus HGM's 64.3% at a 20.8% lower target-cost index.

以上为 arXiv 摘要节选，中文省流版整理中。

item.title: Does self-distillation improve reasoning?
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Self-distillation is an emerging approach that trains a model to imitate its own predictions when conditioned on privileged information, such as correct answers or environmental feedback.

Self-distillation is an emerging approach that trains a model to imitate its own predictions when conditioned on privileged information, such as correct answers or environmental feedback. Recent methods have reported better sample efficiency and generalization than reinforcement learning (RL), but it remains unclear whether these gains extend beyond in-distribution evaluations and whether they stem from privileged distillation. In this paper, we revisit two representative methods, Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (SDPO) and On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), across code, science, tool use, and math reasoning tasks. We find that their reported gains do not consistently generalize to unseen problems and are largely explained by overfitting or transferring existing reasoning behavior, rather than effectively using privileged information. Moreover, self-distillation gradients show weak alignment with policy gradients that directly optimize expected reward, questioning whether they provide an effective direction for policy improvement. Our experiments across Qwen3 models (1.7B-14B) and OLMo-3-7B suggest that effectively leveraging privileged information to improve reasoning remain…

item.title: Does Pretraining Teach Chemical Language Models Chemistry?
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Chemical language models (CLMs) are pretrained on large corpora of molecules with the aim of learning representations that transfer to diverse downstream tasks.

Chemical language models (CLMs) are pretrained on large corpora of molecules with the aim of learning representations that transfer to diverse downstream tasks. Here, we systematically study the effects of pretraining using a series of such CLMs across 64 molecular property prediction datasets. We find that the downstream gains of pretraining in CLMs do not scale and performance saturates below gradient-boosting baselines. Across the regimes evaluated, only supervised pretraining on traditional physico-chemical descriptors consistently improves downstream performance for the CLMs tested whereas some forms of pretraining result in models worse than a randomly initialized encoder. While models can resolve molecular structure well, they do so no better than a randomly initialized model, suggesting that, at best, CLMs learn descriptor-like properties in addition to low-level token statistics during pretraining, but surprisingly little chemistry beyond what classical molecular features already capture.

item.title: DoSA: Dots Sparse Attention
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Sparse attention visits few keys, yet finding them can still require scoring every key with every indexer head.

Sparse attention visits few keys, yet finding them can still require scoring every key with every indexer head. We introduce DoSA (Dots Sparse Attention), a lossless method for making this computation conditional while preserving exact token selection. Its central observation is that Top-K selection requires sufficient evidence to reject a candidate, not necessarily its full score. A seed set supplies a lower bound on the winning threshold. Nonnegative head projections and joint residual bounds upper-bound positive contributions, while activation-informed aggregation bounds the magnitude subtracted by negative heads. The certificate directs full scoring toward candidates that remain eligible; exact-score filtering further reduces writeback and selection work. We establish the certificate and its exact-selection conditions, and analyze how geometry and selection margins govern its effectiveness. Our GPU implementation accelerates the complete Indexer by up to 2.74 times over SGLang and 1.69 times over LiteTopK across English, Chinese, and code workloads. End-to-end evaluation on GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V3.2 achieves up to 1.94 times and 1.50 times time-to-first-token speedups over the …

item.title: Dissecting the Carbon-SLO Tension in Geo-Distributed LLM Serving
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Large Language Model (LLM) inference is driving a growing share of datacenter carbon emissions.

Large Language Model (LLM) inference is driving a growing share of datacenter carbon emissions. Although carbon-aware scheduling can reduce these emissions in geo-distributed datacenters by exploiting the spatiotemporal variations in grid carbon intensity, the latency-sensitive nature of LLM serving constrains this design space. While prior studies investigate the carbon savings achievable through spatial scheduling, they oversimplify the dynamics of modern inference engines, such as queueing and continuous batching, which strongly shape inference latency. We address this issue by designing and evaluating a latency-centric, geo-distributed inference simulator, calibrated with hardware-grounded latency and power measurements, that reproduces these dynamics and enables the study of carbon savings under strict service-level objectives (SLOs). We then formulate a series of SLO- and carbon-aware schedulers of increasing sophistication, from per-request heuristics to batch-level optimization: (i) a greedy heuristic, (ii) an integer linear programming (ILP)-based scheduler jointly assigning batches of requests, (iii) an iterative ILP-based solution projecting its own assignments back into…

item.title: DisaggKD: Efficient Knowledge Distillation through Teacher-Student Disaggregation and a Fused Loss
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Knowledge distillation (KD) frameworks place teacher and student on the same GPUs, so per-GPU memory limits the teachers that fit.

Knowledge distillation (KD) frameworks place teacher and student on the same GPUs, so per-GPU memory limits the teachers that fit. DisaggKD separates them across nodes: teacher replicas stream hidden states to the student, a KD loss over row windows and vocabulary shards equals the full-vocabulary loss in exact arithmetic without forming the full-vocabulary logits, and a prefetch ring paces producer and trainer. Closed-form memory and traffic models locate the memory limits of each layout. On the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B to 9B pair, the disaggregated layout matches the LM loss of the colocated run with the same loss and is faster than that run; our fused loss also lets a colocated run train on as few nodes at faster speed, while the split is memory efficient when the student spans several nodes. On the larger pairs, colocated runs with a fused loss still run OOM where the split trains, because teacher weights and student states fill the budget.

item.description:

Computing equilibria in high-dimensional continuous games requires learning and representing rich, multi-modal strategy distributions, something conventional neural policies struggle to achieve.

Computing equilibria in high-dimensional continuous games requires learning and representing rich, multi-modal strategy distributions, something conventional neural policies struggle to achieve. Diffusion models offer a natural solution, but standard diffusion training requires direct samples from a fixed target distribution, which are generally unavailable under iterative game-solving updates. We propose a diffusion-based framework for equilibrium computation that enables diffusion-based variants of Online Mirror Descent (OMD) and Fictitious Play (FP). Our approach derives a reweighted score-matching objective that trains diffusion policies without requiring direct samples from each updated policy. Our main method, DiffNash, combines the fast convergence of OMD with the sample efficiency of FP by reusing past actions through a replay buffer. Multimodal learning offers the potential to improve predictions by integrating complementary information from heterogeneous data sources.

Multimodal learning offers the potential to improve predictions by integrating complementary information from heterogeneous data sources. However, multimodal datasets are frequently incomplete, raising important questions about how models should handle missing information. Although recent approaches increasingly rely on Transformer-based architectures for multimodal fusion, incomplete multimodal data introduces challenges such as missing modalities and intra-modal missingness, which motivate key architectural design choices, such as tokenization granularity. In addition, many datasets are longitudinal, with observations collected across multiple time points. The sequential nature of the Transformer architectures provides a natural framework for modeling such data, but introduces additional considerations, such as how temporal information should be represented. In this study, we systematically investigate these design choices using three different cancer datasets. item.title: DeKoR: Decomposed Knowledge Routing for Efficient GNN--LLM Fusion
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong potential for text-attributed graph learning by leveraging rich pre-trained knowledge and language understanding capabilities.

Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong potential for text-attributed graph learning by leveraging rich pre-trained knowledge and language understanding capabilities. Combining LLMs with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) offers a promising paradigm for expanding the modeling capabilities of graph learning. However, LLMs and GNNs follow distinct learning paradigms, leading to a pronounced mismatch between their knowledge spaces. Such discrepancies make effective knowledge fusion nontrivial. Moreover, existing methods often incur substantial additional computation for only limited performance gains. To address these challenges, we propose DeKoR, an efficient framework for GNN and LLM knowledge fusion. To enable efficient knowledge transfer, DeKoR decomposes LLM knowledge into complementary local and global views and uses the LLM as an offline teacher to distill them into lightweight experts. To enable selective knowledge fusion, an adaptive router learns how much each node should rely on each expert. The key difficulty is that neural architectures are operation-labeled DAGs: edge direction defines computational flow, but existing predictors often treat direction as a local structural cue. item.title: DRanker: A Transformer-Based Multi-Task Ranking Model for the Disney+ Homepage
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

We present DRanker (Disney+ Ranker), a transformer-based multitask ranking model serving personalized recommendations on the Disney+ homepage.

We present DRanker (Disney+ Ranker), a transformer-based multitask ranking model serving personalized recommendations on the Disney+ homepage. We describe the encoder-only architecture over enriched engagement-history sequences paired with a lightweight causal debiasing mechanism, and the inference stack that enables transformer-based ranking at scale. Through iterative development, we systematically evaluated more complex alternatives and found that simpler designs consistently outperformed them on offline metrics, qualitative behavioral evaluation, and in production. Deployed globally, DRanker drives over 1% lift in our key engagement metric and 0.5% lift in daily active users across all experiences powered by the ranker. We share practical lessons on data engineering, debiasing, and architectural choices that shaped our ranking system at scale.

研究问题：新兴 dataflow 加速器能效高却对开发者不透明，缺少 CPU/GPU 那样的性能分析工具。

方法：提出 DFIT 测量框架，在 graph IR 与后端下沉阶段用语义化程序表示直接对算子、区域和编译变换插桩，捕获反映真实数据流的高层语义数据并导出可视化。

关键数字：在 Cerebras、SambaNova、TPU 三类平台上评估，各插桩模式的实际开销为 3.53%–13.62%，跨平台可移植性良好。

为什么值得看：打开 dataflow 执行的黑盒，为编译器设计、运行时调度与硬件实现之间长期存在的可见性鸿沟提供可复现的架构感知内省基础。

item.title: DEFT: Disentanglement-Enhanced Fine-Tuning for EEG Foundation Models
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

EEG foundation models (EFMs) have improved EEG representation learning by transferring knowledge from large-scale multi-subject pretraining to downstream tasks.

EEG foundation models (EFMs) have improved EEG representation learning by transferring knowledge from large-scale multi-subject pretraining to downstream tasks. However, their pretrained embeddings often retain substantial subject-related variation, placing an additional burden on the downstream classifier, especially in cross-subject settings. To address this issue, we propose Disentangled EFM Fine-Tuning (DEFT), a plug-and-play adapter for EFM fine-tuning. DEFT encourages branch disentanglement of pretrained tokens into task-oriented content and subject-consistent style, then performs downstream prediction from the content branch. It instantiates this factorize-before-classify design with recursive Gaussian refinement, temporal-variance regularization, subject-aware contrastive learning, and reconstruction. Experiments across multiple EEG datasets and four EFM backbones show that DEFT improves matched fine-tuning baselines. Further ablations and analyses support the intended content/style branch organization.

以上为 arXiv 摘要节选，中文省流版整理中。

Model merging combines fine-tuned experts into one network without retraining, and closed-form methods compute each merged layer from statistics of its input activations.

Model merging combines fine-tuned experts into one network without retraining, and closed-form methods compute each merged layer from statistics of its input activations. However, these statistics are measured on a single expert, while in the merged model, each layer receives activations from the merged layers that precede it. Recent work re-measures these statistics in the merged model but still forms them from a single network. We formulate closed-form methods as a linear system and show that they use the same matrix on both sides. We then introduce CrossMean, which replaces this matrix on one side with a bilinear statistic that pairs merged and expert activations. From the same statistics, we also derive a label-free criterion that indicates the task sets in which accounting for the merged activations improves the merge more. Empirically, task sets with a lower criterion value show a larger improvement. On the eight-task benchmark of each vision backbone that we tested and on BERT encoders, CrossMean improves on merging with statistics measured on the experts, and with all linear layers merged, it also improves on re-measuring these statistics in the merged model. Generating realistic time-series requires faithfully reproducing rare but high-impact extreme events.

Generating realistic time-series requires faithfully reproducing rare but high-impact extreme events. Existing approaches often rely on specialized representations or extreme-focused training objectives, which may restrict the diversity of captured extremes or compromise overall distributional fidelity. We propose Cross-View Time-Frequency Diffusion (CrossTF), a framework that exploits discrepancies between time- and frequency-view denoisers for extreme-aware time-series generation. Our key empirical finding is extreme-sensitive cross-view asymmetry: moving along the direction connecting the two views' clean-sample estimates substantially changes extreme fidelity while having limited effects on overall generation quality. We further identify a late-stage cross-view window in which this discrepancy stabilizes and cross-view adjustments have a particularly strong effect on extreme fidelity. item.title: Counting with Attention and LayerNorm: Norm Scaling and Representation Geometry
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Counting is a simple task on which transformers can nevertheless fail at long sequence lengths.

Counting is a simple task on which transformers can nevertheless fail at long sequence lengths. We study the cost of counting in a single attention layer, up to a maximum length $L$, focusing on how softmax attention and layer normalization shape the representation from which the count is recovered. We mainly focus on regression read-out but also consider classification read-out. For regression, we show unnormalized linear attention counts exactly at parameter norms independent of $L$. For softmax attention, regression cannot count exactly with finite parameters; it recovers the count after rounding, but only when the vector parameter norms grow with $L$. We measure this cost by $B_{\min}$, the smallest bound that can be placed on every trainable vector to ensure exact counting after rounding, and derive tight rates. At fixed model dimension, $B_{\min}$ grows as $L$ without normalization, as $L^{3/2}$ under bare post-normalization, and as $L^{3/4}$ with learned post-normalization. The last rate is unexpected: post-normalization discards the magnitude that carries the count and might be expected to make counting harder, yet with a learnable gain it counts at a smaller norm than soft…

item.title: Correcting or Continuing? What On-Policy Distillation Learns from Student Errors
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher, mitigating the distribution mismatch of off-policy supervision.

On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher, mitigating the distribution mismatch of off-policy supervision. While prior work has primarily trained on problems a student can largely solve, we ask whether OPD can improve a student when training is restricted to problems it currently fails. We evaluate five representative OPD mechanisms with Qwen-3 and Phi-4 models under a unified competition-mathematics protocol. We find that OPD does not improve accuracy on this hard subset, with most mechanisms instead degrading performance despite continued decreases in training KL divergence. All eight configurations show a decline, and the two-sided sign test gives p=0.0078. In contrast, the same pipeline improves accuracy by 4.6 percentage points when training is not concentrated on failures, showing that the failure is conditional on the training regime rather than systematic. These findings suggest that OPD is effective when supervision is dominated by correct student prefixes, but can reinforce existing errors when training is concentrated on problems the student currently fails.

item.description:

方法 用不同精度/上下文长度的实测校准时延模型，结合张量敏感度在时延或精度预算下选配置；预测器按校准执行成本而非权重字节估时延；运行时按预生成调度执行并保留会话 KV。

关键数字 摘要未给统一量化结论；在笔记本 GPU 上评测，含三种权重格式的长上下文调度与工具调用基准（完整响应时间与正确率）。

item.title: Constant-Depth Rational-Weight GNNs and their Connection to Schanuel's Conjecture
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

A landmark result states that the expressive power of graph neural networks (GNNs) is bounded from above by the 1-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman (1-WL) test.

A landmark result states that the expressive power of graph neural networks (GNNs) is bounded from above by the 1-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman (1-WL) test. We ask whether a constant-depth GNN can match the expressive power of 1-WL while using only rational weights. We prove that this is the case when Schanuel's conjecture, a famous open problem from transcendental number theory, is taken to be true. Our GNN construction works even with integer weights, and more generally with a broad range of rational weights. As the activation function, it may use logistic sigmoid, hyperbolic tangent, or related functions. It is uniform across all graph sizes. We also prove a partial converse: if a GNN with exponentiation, hyperbolic sine or hyperbolic cosine as activation matches the expressive power of the 1-WL test in a slightly more expressive setting where graphs may contain certain auxiliary vertices, then this implies Schanuel's conjecture restricted to the numbers that arise in computations of the GNN. We also conduct experiments showing that the constructed GNNs indeed match the 1-WL test.

以上为 arXiv 摘要节选，中文省流版整理中。

item.title: Confine to the Task, Anchor the Rest: Concept-Guided Retention Regularizer for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) has been widely used, yet the adapted model suffers catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained knowledge.

Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) has been widely used, yet the adapted model suffers catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained knowledge. While most existing work hardens the adapter by constraining where the weight update may lie, we note that constraining this weight channel does not constrain the activation channel. In this paper, we propose Concept-Guided Retention (CGR), a plug-and-play regularizer that constrains both for any PEFT base. CGR reads a frozen sparse autoencoder (SAE) and treats two disjoint concept sets differently. It softly confines the update to the task-concept subspace (via weight channel), and anchors a selected set of general-purpose concepts to the frozen model (via activation channel). We also provide anchor value bounds based on weight updates to understand how they interact, and show that both terms are necessary. On a CLIP vision panel, CGR significantly improves retention at comparable accuracy for every base, and the same pattern holds for world-knowledge retention under Llama-3.1-8B instruction tuning. Because the protected directions are named SAE concepts, CGR remains inspectable and controllable.

以上为 arXiv 摘要节选，中文省流版整理中。

item.title: Compute-Optimal Scaling Laws for Spiking Language Models
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Spiking neural networks target energy-efficient language modeling through sparse, binary activations, but the efficiency-accuracy tradeoff of spiking language models is uncharacterized at scale.

Spiking neural networks target energy-efficient language modeling through sparse, binary activations, but the efficiency-accuracy tradeoff of spiking language models is uncharacterized at scale. We present the first Chinchilla-style IsoFLOP scaling study of a spiking language model, sweeping SpikeGPT-family models (RWKV backbone) from width 384 to 1536 across compute budgets from $3\times10^{17}$ to $10^{19}$ FLOPs on FineWeb-EDU. We report two findings. First, the compute-optimal frontier is $N_{opt} \propto C^{0.56}$, close to the 0.50 that Hoffmann et al. report for dense Transformers, so spiking does not change how parameters and data should be traded off under a compute budget. Second, against non-spiking RWKV and Transformer baselines trained the same way, the loss gap splits into a backbone cost of about 0.16 nats that does not change with compute and a spiking cost that falls from 0.34 to about 0.23 nats and then levels off. These results give the first compute-optimal recipe for spiking language models and quantify the accuracy cost of their sparsity.

以上为 arXiv 摘要节选，中文省流版整理中。

item.title: Compression Through Time: An Interplay of Separability, Stationarity and Capacity
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Information-theoretic and geometric compression have been widely studied as possible explanations for generalization.

Information-theoretic and geometric compression have been widely studied as possible explanations for generalization. Yet their temporal dynamics in recurrent networks remain largely unexplored. Using discretized LSTMs, whose finite embedding space enables direct estimates of information quantities, we observe pronounced compression across the final timesteps of many datasets. We explain this effect through three competing mechanisms: (i) class separability permits stronger compression at the final timestep; (ii) shared recurrent dynamics propagate this pressure across timesteps with similar activation states, making its extent depend on temporal stationarity; and (iii) limited representational capacity opposes prolonged compression because it restricts information available for subsequent computation. We systematically test these mechanisms through controlled synthetic interventions and real-world sequence tasks. Our results identify class separability, temporal stationarity, and network capacity as key determinants of temporal compression, and suggest that compression acts as a regularizer-potentially beneficial when excess capacity is available, but harmful to generalization whe…

item.title: Compositional Performance Modeling of LLM Inference Clusters with Hierarchical KV Caching
item.description:
发表方：arXiv　发布：2026-10-14　分类：论文PDF

Design-space exploration of LLM inference clusters requires predicting how hardware and serving policies interact with hierarchical key-value (KV) caching.

Design-space exploration of LLM inference clusters requires predicting how hardware and serving policies interact with hierarchical key-value (KV) caching. Isolated operation profiles alone do not determine cluster latency: reuse changes computational demand, while KV location, capacity, and contention govern execution order. We present a compositional discrete-event simulator based on separating local service costs from shared resource and KV availability. Compute and transfer models calibrated on one-prefill/one-decode (1P-1D) deployments are reused across compatible workers, enabling policy and topology comparisons without per-configuration latency fitting. Validation against SGLang covers Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B on 1P-1D and 3P-1D clusters. Mean request end-to-end latency error is 1.34% for question answering and 6.36% for captured coding sessions, measured as mean absolute percentage error. CPU simulation reduces replay turnaround by 15.33 times on average; real replay includes prescribed arrival gaps. Measured session-affinity and simulated retention studies demonstrate how the framework guides policy selection by predicting the joint effects on computation, latency, and KV oc…
